title: cooperative-token-pacing-and-kernel-coalescing-to-stabilize-streaming-tail-latency
author: Maya Ortega
description:
Motivation: P50 improvements from prior microbatching and probabilistic flush changes have been good but customers still report noisy p99s on sustained multiplexed streaming workloads. This PR introduces a cooperative token pacing controller, kernel coalescing for short-kernel bursts, and a lightweight KV prefetch strategy to smooth out flush storms and reduce kernel launch overhead.
What changed: 1) runtime/scheduling: extracted a pacing controller (scheduler/pacing.rs) that tracks per-request token credits and emits 'soft' pacing signals to the token emitter; 2) token loop: refactored token_emitter.rs to separate emission, flush scheduling, and backpressure hooks so pacing can 'steer' microflush windows; 3) kernel coalescer: new native module (kernels/coalescer.cu + kernels/coalescer.h) that coalesces adjacent small kernels into a single launch when dependencies allow; 4) KV cache prefetch: heuristic pre-warm in kv/cache_prefetch.rs that issues inexpensive cache-lookups for hot key ranges predicted by the pacing controller; 5) tests & benchmarks: new bench/bench_streaming_latency.py and e2e integration test (tests/streaming_stress_test.go); 6) documentation: perf notes and tuning guide at docs/perf/streaming-pacing.md.
Benchmarks: microbench on p4d: steady-state throughput unchanged, median inter-token latency reduced ~10%, median first-byte ~6% lower, p99 tail improved 18-32% across mixes used in ENG-4821. End-to-end service canary saw reduced bursty spikes under multiplexing workloads.
Commits summary: - a1b2c3: add pacing controller + interfaces - d4e5f6: refactor token emitter and wire pacing hooks - 7g8h9i: implement kernel coalescer and CUDA unit tests - j0k1l2: KV prefetch heuristic + metrics - m3n4o5: add benches, docs, and integration tests.
Changed files (high-level): runtime/token_emitter.rs, scheduler/pacing.rs, kernels/coalescer.cu, kernels/coalescer.h, kv/cache_prefetch.rs, bench/bench_streaming_latency.py, tests/streaming_stress_test.go, docs/perf/streaming-pacing.md, ci/ci_streaming.yml, examples/streaming_tuning.toml.
Review conversation: Reviewer Aaron Park: "Can you quantify the coalescer decision latency? worried about added scheduling jitter." Author (Maya): "Coalescer decision is O(1) on critical path; added microbench in coalescer unit test and included comments in kernels/coalescer.h; see commit 7g8h9i." Reviewer Sofia Patel: "KV prefetch risks thrashing under unpredictable inputs." Author: "Prefetch is gated by credit windows and only targets top-5 predicted keys per request; added opt-out env var and metric 'kv_prefetch_miss_ratio'." Reviewer Noah Rivera: "Please add a fallthrough path when coalescing cannot proceed to avoid head-of-line delays." Author: "Added fallthrough and explicit timers to avoid >2ms stall; see token_emitter.rs change." Approvals: Aaron approved after one small comment, Sofia requested one change which was addressed, Noah gave final approval.
CI summary: Linux unit tests passed, CUDA unit tests passed on CI runners, integration e2e had a flaky test that failed once and was retried; final CI green. All checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), cuda-tests (pass), bench-smoke (pass), lint (pass).
Merge: Squash merged into main on 2026-03-02 by Maya Ortega after approvals. Release notes: "Stabilize streaming tail latency with cooperative token pacing and kernel coalescing; recommend enabling kv_prefetch on dedicated pools for multiplexed traffic; see docs/perf/streaming-pacing.md for tuning"
